DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF A HIGH-FREQUENCY CORONA DISCHARGE OZONATOR FOR DRINKING WATER PURIFICATION

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Maxat Mamadiyarov, Kanat Zhunussov, Yerlan Tashtay, Gulbakhar Yussupova, Almukhan Nuraliyev, Bulgyn Mailykhanova, Yasir Igisi mbayev, Nazym Zhakupova, Ayaulym Bilal, Aikenzhe Rakhim

ABSTRACT

In this work, we study the optimization of the operating parameters of the corona discharge method to increase ozone production and reduce the energy consumption, especially for water purification. Water pollution is one of the most important ecological problems of the present time, and ozone is widely used as a safe and effective water treatment method. In this work, the parameters of the corona discharge system were tuned to enhance the ozone concentration in water up to 40 mg/L and reduce the energy consumption by 15%. In particular, the optimal conditions of 30 kV voltage, 25 kHz pulse frequency, and 40 µs pulse duration led to the highest ozone concentration and improved energy efficiency. The energy consumption for ozone generation was 5-8 mg/kWh, which was significantly lower than that reported in previous studies. These results demonstrate the potential of the corona discharge system as an energy efficient solution for large scale water purification. The study shows that ozone production can be enhanced and energy consumption reduced with the optimization of the operational parameters, leading to more sustainable and efficient water treatment technologies.
